_note: Original advanced concept questions for recursion.

questions.title: Base case
questions.prompt: What is the job of a base case?
questions.explanation: The base case handles the smallest input without making another recursive call.

questions.title: Smaller input
questions.code:
factorial(4)
-> 4 * factorial(3)
-> 3 is closer to the base case
questions.prompt: Why should a recursive call use a smaller or simpler input?
choices: So it moves toward the base case
So it uses more memory forever
questions.explanation: The call must make progress toward stopping.

questions.title: Trace factorial
questions.explanation: The calls return 1, then 2 * 1, then 3 * 2, which is 6.

questions.title: Infinite recursion
questions.prompt: What is wrong with `return n * factorial(n)` inside factorial?
choices: The input does not get smaller.
questions.explanation: Calling with the same n repeats the same problem and never reaches the base case.

questions.title: Recursive sum
questions.prompt: Arrange the steps for recursively summing a list.
lines: If the list is empty, return 0.
Recursively sum the rest of the list.
Return first value plus the smaller sum.
questions.explanation: The base case handles empty input; the recursive step adds one value to the answer for the smaller list.

questions.title: Call stack
questions.code:
Waiting calls:
factorial(3)
  waits for factorial(2)
    waits for factorial(1)
questions.prompt: Where do unfinished recursive calls wait?
questions.explanation: Each call waits on the call stack until the smaller call returns.

questions.title: Tree recursion
questions.prompt: A tree height function calls itself on left and right children. What combines the two answers?
questions.explanation: Height counts the current node plus the taller child path.

questions.title: Recursion cost
questions.code:
fib(5)
-> fib(4) + fib(3)
-> fib(3) gets computed again
questions.prompt: Why can naive recursive Fibonacci be slow?
choices: It recomputes the same smaller answers many times.
It has no base case at all.
questions.explanation: Many calls repeat the same Fibonacci values unless you store or avoid repeated work.
